In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-ingress-operator/pull/1508): >> **Note**: This is the second attempt. First attempt was #1456, which was reverted in #1507. > >## Summary > >Vendors the sail-operator install library from the OSSM 3.4 release branch and adapts CIO to the updated API. > >- **Vendor sail library** from `openshift-service-mesh/sail-operator` release-3.4 >- **Adapt to API changes** in the 3.4 install library ([upstream](https://github.com/istio-ecosystem/sail-operator/pull/1857), [downstream backport](https://github.com/openshift-service-mesh/sail-operator/pull/901)) — new function signatures, CRD ownership model, values defaults >- **Bump OSSM version to 3.4.0** and Istio version to `v1.28-latest` (resolves to the latest 1.28 patch available in the catalog) >- **Add unit test** (`TestSailLibraryImageDigestsAreDownstream`) to catch upstream images slipping through — the sail library silently defaults to `registry.istio.io` images, and we've been tricked by this before > >## Known changes from the upstream install library > >### API changes > >- `install.New()` now takes a third argument `chart.CRDsFS` (the CRD filesystem) and variadic `LibraryOption` args. >- `install.Start()` now returns `(<-chan struct{}, error)` instead of just `<-chan struct{}`. >- `install.Apply()` now returns `error` instead of being void. >- `install.MergeValues()` now returns `(*sailv1.Values, error)` instead of just `*sailv1.Values`. >- `install.GatewayAPIDefaults()` now takes a `namespace` string argument. >- `install.Options.ManageCRDs` and `IncludeAllCRDs` changed from `*bool` to `bool`. > >### CRD ownership / labeling > >- CRDs continue to be labeled with `ingress.operator.openshift.io/owned=true` via `WithCRDOwnershipLabel`. This preserves backward compatibility with the old library and the origin upgrade test. > >### Status conditions (CRDsReady) > >The 3.4 sail library replaced ownership-based CRD states with readiness-based states and per-CRD `Managed`/`Ready` booleans. The `CRDInfo` struct now uses `Managed bool` and `Ready bool` fields instead of a single `State` enum. CIO maps these back to preserve the original condition reasons by inspecting per-CRD ownership via `countManagedCRDs`. > >| Old reason | New reason | Status | Message change | >|---|---|---|---| >| `ManagedByCIO` | `ManagedByCIO` | `True` | No change (removed from library, now set by CIO) | >| `ManagedByOLM` | `ManagedByOLM` | `True` | No change (removed from library, now set by CIO) | >| `MixedOwnership` | `MixedOwnership` | `True` (was `False`) | The library reports `Ready` when CRDs are established regardless of ownership; `False` was incorrect | >| `NoneExist` | `NoneExist` | `Unknown` | No change | >| `UnknownManagement` | `UnknownManagement` | `False` | No change | >| — | `NotReady` | `False` | New. Per-CRD list can include `(not ready)` suffix | >| — | `Error` | `False` | New. Per-CRD list can include `(not ready)` suffix | > >All existing condition reasons and messages are preserved. `MixedOwnership` status changed from `False` to `True` since the library reports CRDs as ready regardless of ownership. `NotReady` and `Error` are additive — the old library had no equivalents. > >### Values defaults > >- `GatewayAPIDefaults()` was significantly stripped down in 3.4 — it now only sets 3 pilot env vars plus namespace and trust bundle. Fields previously set by `GatewayAPIDefaults` (`AccessLogFile`, `IngressControllerMode`, `ProxyHeaders`) are now set in CIO's `openshiftValues()`. > >### Unit test changes > >- Removed `TestOLMAndSailLibraryValuesMatch` — the 3.4 sail library makes it difficult to compute real effective values in a unit test since profiles and defaults are applied internally via `ComputeValues`. The same coverage is provided by `Test_Reconcile` which already verifies the full `install.Options` for both OLM and sail library paths. Instructions for interacting with me using PR comments are available [here](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/command-help?repo=openshift%2Fcluster-ingress-operator). If you have questions or suggestions related to my behavior, please file an issue against the [openshift-eng/jira-lifecycle-plugin](https://github.com/openshift-eng/jira-lifecycle-plugin/issues/new) repository.

## Verdict

The statement is **not correct as a literal or behavioral equivalence claim**: `#1508` is **not the same patch** as `#1456`.

- `#1456` stable patch ID: `aa06cc03e1d595dd36c6d63d78933c2428121dd6`
- `#1508` stable patch ID: `21ac7610528a6b2e83f8e38991aa78207eb0954b`
- `#1456`: **2,996 files**, `+266,653/-145,690`
- `#1508`: **3,238 files**, `+298,005/-154,131`

They do share the central migration from the older Sail install API to the OSSM 3.4 API, but `#1508` contains additional fixes and preserves several unrelated ingress/operator behaviors that `#1456` removed.

## Changes shared by both PRs

These core Sail migration changes are carried forward:

- Gateway API operator version: `servicemeshoperator3.v3.3.1` → `servicemeshoperator3.v3.4.0`.
- Istio version: `v1.28.5` → `v1.28-latest`.
- `install.New()` receives `chart.CRDsFS` and the CIO CRD ownership label.
- `installer.Start()` is error-checked.
- `SailLibraryInstaller.Start()` returns `(<-chan struct{}, error)`.
- `SailLibraryInstaller.Apply()` returns `error`.
- The updated install-library API/values/status tests are substantially shared.

For the common paths that do not appear in the per-file mismatch list, Git’s stable patch comparison found the PR changes equivalent.

## `#1508` additions absent from `#1456`

### 1. Updated Sail library fixes

`#1508` vendors a meaningfully different Sail implementation:

- **Lifecycle mutex fix** in `vendor/github.com/istio-ecosystem/sail-operator/pkg/install/library.go` and `vendor/github.com/istio-ecosystem/sail-operator/pkg/install/reconciler.go`.
  - Adds `lifecycleMu`.
  - Serializes `Apply`, reconciliation, and `Uninstall`.
  - Prevents an in-flight reconciliation from reinstalling Istio after an uninstall.

- **TLS/PQC support** in `vendor/github.com/istio-ecosystem/sail-operator/pkg/istiovalues/tls.go`.
  - Clears cipher suites when TLS 1.3 is the minimum protocol, because Envoy does not support explicit cipher-suite configuration in that case.
  - Reads OpenShift TLS profile groups and maps curve aliases—such as `secp256r1` → `P-256`—to Envoy-compatible ECDH curve names.
  - Applies those curves to Istio TLS defaults.

- **TLS security-profile watcher leader-election change** in `vendor/github.com/openshift/controller-runtime-common/pkg/tls/controller.go`.
  - Configures the watcher with `NeedLeaderElection: false`.

These are actual implementation differences, not patch-context differences.

### 2. Five updated generated CRD manifests

Only `#1508` changes:

- `manifests/00-custom-resource-definition.yaml`
- `manifests/00-custom-resource-definition-CustomNoUpgrade.yaml`
- `manifests/00-custom-resource-definition-DevPreviewNoUpgrade.yaml`
- `manifests/00-custom-resource-definition-OKD.yaml`
- `manifests/00-custom-resource-definition-TechPreviewNoUpgrade.yaml`

The changes include:

- AWS Network Load Balancer `protocol` support (`TCP`/`PROXY`) in spec and status.
- TLS `groups` support, including PQC/hybrid groups such as `X25519MLKEM768`.
- Updated TLS profile documentation/default groups and Mozilla TLS guidance.
- Replacing `maxConnections` OpenAPI `anyOf` validation with CEL:
  `self == 0 || self == -1 || (self >= 2000 && self <= 2000000)`.

Those changes alone mean `#1508` cannot be considered the same PR as `#1456`.

### 3. Dependency refresh differences

`#1508` has a broader dependency/vendor refresh, including the Go toolchain bump to `1.25.7` and updated OpenShift/Kubernetes/Gateway API dependency content. This accounts for much of the additional vendor delta.

## `#1456` changes absent from `#1508`

`#1456` removes or changes several behaviors that `#1508` does **not** remove. These are real PR-level differences; several use the same pre-change blob in both PRs, so they cannot be explained solely by differing branch bases.

### GatewayClass OLM behavior

In `pkg/operator/controller/gatewayclass/controller.go`, `#1456` additionally:

- Removes `Config.OperatorLifecycleManagerEnabled`.
- Makes Subscription and InstallPlan watches unconditional instead of conditional on OLM capability.

`#1508` retains the capability-gated behavior and only applies the Sail API adaptation.

### Router/HAProxy architecture rollback

`#1456` removes the HAProxy sidecar/init-container model and associated configuration from:

- `pkg/manifests/assets/router/deployment.yaml`
- `pkg/operator/controller/ingress/deployment.go`
- `pkg/operator/controller/ingress/deployment_test.go`
- `manifests/02-deployment.yaml`
- `manifests/02-deployment-ibm-cloud-managed.yaml`
- `manifests/image-references`

Specifically, `#1456` removes the init-router and HAProxy sidecar containers, HAProxy config volume, service-account projected volume, socket handling, sidecar resource checks, and related deployment-hash coverage. `#1508` retains those behaviors.

### Status controller / orphaned Subscription behavior

`#1456` removes functionality that `#1508` preserves in:

- `pkg/operator/controller/status/controller.go`
- `pkg/operator/controller/status/controller_test.go`
- `manifests/0000_90_ingress-operator_03_prometheusrules.yaml`
- `cmd/ingress-operator/start.go`

The removed `#1456` behavior includes:

- The `ingress_operator_orphaned_ossm_subscription` metric.
- Registration of that metric at startup.
- The `OrphanedOSSMSubscription` Prometheus alert.
- Detection and degraded-condition reporting for CIO-owned orphaned OSSM subscriptions after migration.
- Related-object entries for RBAC resources and ingress component routes.
- Some capability-aware Marketplace/OLM gating logic.

`#1508` retains these behaviors.

### E2E test and network-tool changes

`#1456` also changes/removes tests and tooling that `#1508` retains, including:

- `nft` → `iptables` setup for `TestConnectTimeout`.
- Router-pod lookup/retry behavior in logging tests.
- Test network-policy setup/cleanup.
- Related helper changes in `test/e2e/operator_test.go`, `test/e2e/util_test.go`, and `test/http/serve-delay-connect.go`.

### Other `#1456-only` removals

`#1456` additionally changes files that `#1508` leaves untouched, including:

- `.ci-operator.yaml` and `Dockerfile` rollback from the 5.0/Go 1.26 builder images to 4.22/Go 1.25 images.
- `OWNERS` removal.
- IBM Cloud/PowerVS CredentialsRequest labels and release-inclusion annotations.
- ClusterOperator RBAC related-object declarations.

## Conclusion

A precise characterization would be:

> `#1508` carries forward the main Sail install-library migration from `#1456`, but it is a newer and materially different implementation. It includes additional Sail lifecycle/TLS/PQC/leader-election fixes and CRD schema updates, while retaining multiple ingress, status, OLM, and e2e behaviors that `#1456` removed.

Therefore, I would **not** use “the same PR” for review or risk assessment. The shared migration can be reviewed as a continuation of `#1456`, but the differences above require independent review and validation.

>## Summary

>- **Vendor sail library** from `openshift-service-mesh/sail-operator` release-3.4

>- **Add unit test** (`TestSailLibraryImageDigestsAreDownstream`) to catch upstream images slipping through — the sail library silently defaults to `registry.istio.io` images, and we've been tricked by this before
>
>## Known changes from the upstream install library
>
>### API changes
>
>- `install.New()` now takes a third argument `chart.CRDsFS` (the CRD filesystem) and variadic `LibraryOption` args.
>- `install.Start()` now returns `(<-chan struct{}, error)` instead of just `<-chan struct{}`.
>- `install.Apply()` now returns `error` instead of being void.
>- `install.MergeValues()` now returns `(*sailv1.Values, error)` instead of just `*sailv1.Values`.
>- `install.GatewayAPIDefaults()` now takes a `namespace` string argument.
>- `install.Options.ManageCRDs` and `IncludeAllCRDs` changed from `*bool` to `bool`.
>
>### CRD ownership / labeling
>
>- CRDs continue to be labeled with `ingress.operator.openshift.io/owned=true` via `WithCRDOwnershipLabel`. This preserves backward compatibility with the old library and the origin upgrade test.
>
>### Status conditions (CRDsReady)
>
>The 3.4 sail library replaced ownership-based CRD states with readiness-based states and per-CRD `Managed`/`Ready` booleans. The `CRDInfo` struct now uses `Managed bool` and `Ready bool` fields instead of a single `State` enum. CIO maps these back to preserve the original condition reasons by inspecting per-CRD ownership via `countManagedCRDs`.
>
>| Old reason | New reason | Status | Message change |
>|---|---|---|---|
>| `ManagedByCIO` | `ManagedByCIO` | `True` | No change (removed from library, now set by CIO) |
>| `ManagedByOLM` | `ManagedByOLM` | `True` | No change (removed from library, now set by CIO) |
>| `MixedOwnership` | `MixedOwnership` | `True` (was `False`) | The library reports `Ready` when CRDs are established regardless of ownership; `False` was incorrect |
>| `NoneExist` | `NoneExist` | `Unknown` | No change |
>| `UnknownManagement` | `UnknownManagement` | `False` | No change |
>| — | `NotReady` | `False` | New. Per-CRD list can include `(not ready)` suffix |
>| — | `Error` | `False` | New. Per-CRD list can include `(not ready)` suffix |
>
>All existing condition reasons and messages are preserved. `MixedOwnership` status changed from `False` to `True` since the library reports CRDs as ready regardless of ownership. `NotReady` and `Error` are additive — the old library had no equivalents.
>
>### Values defaults
>
>- `GatewayAPIDefaults()` was significantly stripped down in 3.4 — it now only sets 3 pilot env vars plus namespace and trust bundle. Fields previously set by `GatewayAPIDefaults` (`AccessLogFile`, `IngressControllerMode`, `ProxyHeaders`) are now set in CIO's `openshiftValues()`.
>
>### Unit test changes
>
>- Removed `TestOLMAndSailLibraryValuesMatch` — the 3.4 sail library makes it difficult to compute real effective values in a unit test since profiles and defaults are applied internally via `ComputeValues`. The same coverage is provided by `Test_Reconcile` which already verifies the full `install.Options` for both OLM and sail library paths.

</details>
